paper.title: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with reward distributions supported in [0,1]
unmapped: Paper remarks Theorems 1-3 also hold when rewards are dependent across arms and only E[X_{i,t}|X_{i,1..t-1}] = mu_i is required
settings.definition_quote: a K-armed bandit problem is defined by random variables X_{i,n} for 1 <= i <= K and n >= 1 ... Successive plays of machine i yield rewards X_{i,1}, X_{i,2}, ... which are independent and identically distributed according to an unknown law with unknown expectation mu_i.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with support in [0,1], known lower bound d on the gaps (epsilon_n-GREEDY)
unmapped: Guarantee is on the instantaneous probability of choosing a suboptimal arm at round n
settings.definition_quote: if policy epsilon_n-GREEDY is run with input parameter 0 < d <= min_{i:mu_i<mu*} Delta_i

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with normally distributed rewards, unknown means and variances
unmapped: Rewards Gaussian with unknown means AND unknown variances (not known-variance Gaussian)
settings.definition_quote: the bandit problem with normally distributed rewards ... when both the mean and the variance of the reward distributions are unknown

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB1 is run on K machines having arbitrary reward distributions P1,...,PK with support in [0,1], then its expected regret after any number n of plays is at most 8 \sum_{i:\mu_i<\mu^*} \ln n/\Delta_i + (1+\pi^2/3)\sum_{j=1}^K \Delta_j

results.notes: Regret defined via expected pull counts (pseudo-regret). Holds for any n.

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB2 is run with input 0 < α < 1 on K machines having arbitrary reward distributions P1,...,PK with support in [0,1], then its expected regret after any number n >= max_{i:mu_i<mu*} 1/(2Delta_i^2) of plays is at most \sum_{i:\mu_i<\mu^*} ( (1+α)(1+4α) ln(2e n Δ_i^2)/(2Δ_i) + c_α/Δ_i )

results.notes: Proof uses alpha < 1/10 at one step though theorem states 0<alpha<1. Formula reconstructed from lossy PDF text.

bound.regime: n >= cK/d (proof uses n >= cK/d^2), 0 < d <= min gap

symbols.d_gap: input parameter d, a lower bound on the minimum gap (0<d<1)
symbols.c_alg: input exploration constant c > 0 of epsilon_n-GREEDY

source.quote: For all K > 1 and for all reward distributions P1,...,PK with support in [0,1], if policy εn-GREEDY is run with input parameter 0 < d ≤ min_{i:µi<µ*} Δi, then the probability that after any number n ≥ cK/d of plays εn-GREEDY chooses a suboptimal machine j is at most ...

results.notes: Bound is on the probability that a given suboptimal arm j is chosen at round n (instantaneous), not cumulative regret; T denotes the round index n. Remark: order c/(d^2 n)+o(1/n) for c>5.

extra_assumptions: Proof relies on Conjectures 1 and 2 (tail bounds for Student and chi-square distributions) verified only numerically

source.quote: For all K > 1, if policy UCB1-NORMAL is run on K machines having normal reward distributions P1,...,PK, then its expected regret after any number n of plays is at most 256(log n) \sum_{i:µi<µ*} σ_i^2/Δ_i + (1 + π^2/2 + 8 log n) \sum_{j=1}^K Δ_j

results.notes: Conditional on numerically verified conjectures. Gaussian with unknown variance mapped to subgaussian noise.
